2609.20186.title: To Copy or Not to Copy: Controlling Speculative Decoding via Intrinsic Model Signals
2609.20186.paper_summary: Speculative Decoding (SD) has significantly accelerated Large Language Model (LLM) inference, yet existing approaches face a fundamental tradeoff between two drafting strategies: neural drafting and context-based copying. Neural drafts (e.g., EAGLE3) provide robust performance across diverse text settings, while copy-based methods achieve higher speedups in copy-intensive regimes by generating candidates faster and exploiting long repetition spans for near-perfect speculation. We analyze existing copy-based methods and find that they are prone to accidental repetitions where surface-level n-gram overlap does not reflect a structural intent to copy, leading to false-positive triggers that ultimately degrade throughput. We introduce SwitchSD, an adaptive framework that treats copying as a latent control signal of the LLM. By training lightweight probes on the target model's internal representations, SwitchSD identifies genuine copy-intent with high precision (AUC > 0.99). This allows the system to dynamically switch between neural drafting (e.g., EAGLE) and context-based copying. Our results across Llama and Qwen families demonstrate throughput gains of up to 15% over state-of-the-art baselines like EAGLE3, effectively turning copying from a noisy heuristic into a principled, model-aware decoding regime.
2609.20186.paper_summary_zh: 推測解碼（SD）顯著加速了大型語言模型（LLM）的推理，但現有方法在兩種草擬策略之間面臨根本的權衡：神經草擬和基於上下文的複製。神經草擬（例如，EAGLE3）在各種文本設置中提供了穩健的性能，而基於複製的方法在複製密集的環境中通過更快地生成候選項和利用長重複範圍來實現更高的加速，從而達到近乎完美的推測。我們分析了現有的基於複製的方法，發現它們容易出現意外重複的情況，其中表面層的n-gram重疊並不反映出複製的結構意圖，導致誤報觸發，最終降低了吞吐量。我們引入了SwitchSD，一個自適應框架，將複製視為LLM的潛在控制信號。通過在目標模型的內部表示上訓練輕量級探針，SwitchSD以高精度（AUC > 0.99）識別真正的複製意圖。這使得系統能夠在神經草擬（例如，EAGLE）和基於上下文的複製之間動態切換。我們在Llama和Qwen系列中的結果顯示，吞吐量比最先進的基準（如EAGLE3）提高了多達15%，有效地將複製從一種嘈雜的啟發式轉變為一種有原則的、模型感知的解碼模式。
